title: 1990 AMC 8 Problem 4
statement: Which of the following could not be the units digit [one’s digit] of the square of a whole number?

solutions.text:
The units digit of a square is determined by the units digit of the number squared. Squaring \(0\) through \(9\) gives units digits \(0,\) \(1,\) \(4,\) \(9,\) \(6,\) \(5,\) \(6,\) \(9,\) \(4,\) \(1\).

So a square can only end in \(0,\) \(1,\) \(4,\) \(5,\) \(6,\) or \(9\); it can never end in \(2,\) \(3,\) \(7,\) or \(8\). Among the choices, only \(8\) is impossible.

Thus, the correct answer is E .
hints: The units digit of a square depends only on the units digit of the number being squared
Square each of the digits \(0\) through \(9\) and record only the units digit of each result
